messages:
elaine: FYI — PhoenixPay wants a POC to replace their current vendor with Redwood. Main asks: prompt parity, token billing mapping, and SOC-like checklist. Can @mike_eng and @ashley_sec join?

mike_eng: On it. Do we have their sample traffic? latency targets?

elaine: They sent two example payloads (short chat + multi-turn form extraction). SLA: p95 < 400ms, burst up to 200 rps. They're sensitive to output diffs on our tokenizer. I'll drop samples in GDrive.

sara_se: Heads up — legal flagged data residency + KMS. They'll require audit logs for 12 months and ability to bring keys.

ashley_sec: KMS + VPC is doable via Private. Need to confirm if they need air-gapped. Also will send a prefilled security questionnaire (NDA already done).

joan_sre: For the POC we can stand up a Dedicated pool in staging. Suggest enabling KV-prefix caching and a 1.7-bit quantized variant to save cost. Will need their CIDR for firewall rules.

mike_eng: About prompt parity — competitor exposes a single `generate` endpoint that accepts `prompt` + `temperature`. Our API distinguishes `chat` vs `completion`. We should map `generate` -> `chat.completions` with system prompt shim. Sample shim:

```: // Competitor -> Redwood mapping
POST /v1/generate
body: {prompt, temperature}
=> POST /v1/chat/completions
body: {messages:[{role:"system",content: "<compat-shim>"},{role:"user",content: prompt}], temperature}
```

mike_eng: We should also normalize role tokens and strip competitor-specific stop sequences to avoid truncation differences.

elaine: Pricing questions — PhoenixPay asked how token billing maps to their current monthly cap. They currently pay per-request with a 1M requests cap.

sara_se: We should provide an estimated token-per-request from their samples and propose a committed spend for Dedicated. Also outline burst pricing for overages.

ashley_sec: Action: I'll fill the PSG security questionnaire by EOD Thursday. Need contact for their infra team to get IPs and KMS metadata.

elaine: Contact is ben@phoenixpay.com. Ben can provide sample IP ranges. I'll ask for the test API key that hits their current vendor so we can replay.

joan_sre: For latency SLO, recommend colocating staging in us-west-2. Also we need to enable structured logging for PII flags. That may need opt-in from customer.

mike_eng: One blocker: PhoenixPay's prompts rely on vendor-specific tokenizers that merge non-ASCII differently. Quick mitigation: run tokenization diff and add a normalization step in the shim to replace problematic characters.

elaine: Timeline proposal — week1: replay + smoke tests; week2: parity eval + security review; week3: scale test and pricing sign-off. Are we aligned?

ashley_sec: Aligned. I'll also request their SOC/ISO certs and add to the security questionnaire answers.

sara_se: Legal wants a short clause on output ownership and reverse-engineering in the SOW — I'll draft.

mike_eng: I'll create a small compatibility harness (open-sourced) that shows request/response diffs and can run locally against their key.

elaine: Perfect. I'll schedule a sync with PhoenixPay for tomorrow 10am PST and invite everyone. Thanks all :thumbsup: 

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: staging-dedicated-pool-v0.2 on 2024-05-02 03:00 UTC

elaine: Note — Ben asked about fallback behavior if we hit capacity: do we return 503 or route to cheaper model? We should confirm a policy.

joan_sre: Default: 503 + automatic retry policy; can add fallback to a cheaper quantized variant if customer agrees. I'll document options.

elaine: Great. Captured. I'll post the action items in the CRM thread after the sync.
